title: sse: fix partial-JSON delimiter ordering and token/event framing in streaming outputs
author: Aisha Banerjee
description:
Motivation: Streaming SSE payloads produced by the OpenAI-compat and native streaming paths occasionally produced improperly ordered delimiter tokens and truncated partial-JSON chunks when clients consumed events at high throughput. This caused downstream parsers (and our Python/TS SDK streaming helpers) to receive out-of-order token/event boundaries and malformed partial JSON fragments, which in turn led to parse errors and customer-facing instability for long-running streams.

What this PR does: updated the SSE framing and chunking logic to guarantee delimiter ordering and token-event pairing across the streaming pipeline. Changes apply to both the native runtime encoder and the OpenAI compatibility layer so behavior is consistent regardless of gateway path. Key fixes: ensure delimiter tokens ("\n" separators and explicit event delimiters) are emitted before any partial JSON token boundary markers; make the token event emitter idempotent under fast-produce slow-consume scenarios; tighten KV-cache flush/emit ordering to avoid interleaving unrelated frames when batching; add defensive buffering and unit tests for partial JSON reconstruction.

High level changes (single-line per commit in description area):
- Framing: guarantee delimiter-first emission ordering in framing.go and delimiter.go
- Encoder: atomically assemble SSE events in encoder.go to avoid interleaving from concurrent goroutines
- OpenAI compat: unify streaming adapter to reuse the same framing primitives and enforce contract expectations
- SDK helpers: update Python/TS helpers to tolerate and reassemble partial JSON chunks if a delimiter boundary is delayed (backcompat with older clients)
- Tests: new end-to-end tests that simulate slow consumers and interleaved batches to validate reconstruction logic

Notes: The description above is presented as a single continuous string to match PR content conventions. See commits/files below for specifics and test evidence.
